 Judgment
The claimant not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MCOP No.4195 of 2019, dated 21.04.2023 has preferred this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

2.The case of the petitioner is that on 05.05.2019 at about 19.15 hours, when the petitioner was a pillion rider in a two wheeler bearing Regn. No.PY-01 AL-7221 at Tindivanam to Villupuram NH-45 Salai, near Kannigapuram Bharath Petrol bunk, proceeding from west to east direction, at that time,
a car bearing Regn. No. TN-07-BJ-2184 coming in the north to south was driven in a rash and negligent manner with great high speed, hit the petitioner's two wheeler and caused an accident.
Due to which, the claimant sustained injuries, for which he underwent treatment in the hospital.
Under these circumstances, the claim petition came to be filed before the Tribunal seeking for payment of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/06/2025 02:27:22 pm )

3.The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, came to a conclusion that the accident had taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the 1st respondent.

Having come to such a conclusion, the Tribunal fixed the total compensation payable at Rs.1,82,300/- under various heads as follows:

sentences.text: On perusal of award passed by the Tribunal below, the fact reveals that the accident was happened in the year 2019 and the claimant was working as a photographer.
So, the notional income was fixed for one month.

On considering the injuries as well as treatment period, the learned Tribunal fixed one month for loss of income, but the learned counsel for appellant argues that due to the injuries sustained, he was not able to move outside and nearly about six months, he was not able to move and could not attend his work.
But, the learned Tribunal had fixed one month for loss of income, however, on seeing the grievous injury, this Court is inclined to modify the period for loss of income as six months.
The accident was happened in the year 2019 and disability was https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 13/06/2025 02:27:22 pm ) fixed at 10%, for which a sum of Rs.5000/- was fixed for per percentage.

Therefore, on considering the cost of living, this Court is inclined to enhance the notional income from Rs.12,000/- to Rs.15,000/- per month and towards disability of 10%, it is to be enhanced from Rs.5000/- to Rs.7000/- per percentage.
As the petitioner sustained injuries and suffered disability, he would have been in need of Nutrition expenses.
Hence, the nutrition expenses is enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
Considering the fact that the petitioner took treatment in the hospital for more than 5 days, he would have required the services of an attender, it has been increased from Rs.2,500/- to Rs.10,000/-.
The petitioner has to do his work with difficulty and he may suffer life long troubles due to the accident.
Hence, he would forego certain amenities at present and future.
Hence, it has been enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
The compensation that has been fixed under the other heads are reasonable and does not require the interference of this Court.

7.In the light of the above discussion, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is modified as follows:

8.The compensation awarded by the tribunal at Rs.1,82,300/- is enhanced to Rs.3,47,730/-.

The second respondent insurance company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.3,47,730/-, less the amount already deposited, together with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/06/2025 02:27:22 pm ) judgment.
Insofar as the enhanced compensation is concerned, the deficit court fee, if not paid, shall be paid by the claimants.
The other directions issued by the Tribunal with regard to the mode of payment of compensation remains unaltered.
It goes without saying that the enhanced compensation that is paid by the Insurance Company can be recovered from the owner of the vehicle as was ordered by the Tribunal.
9.In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.
